  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models</h1>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models leverage pretrained Vision–Language Models (VLMs) as backbones to map images and instructions to actions, demonstrating remarkable potential for generalizable robotic manipulation. To enhance performance, existing methods often incorporate extra observation cues (e.g., depth maps, point clouds) or auxiliary modules (e.g., object detectors, encoders) to enable more precise and reliable task execution, yet these typically require costly data collection and additional training. Inspired by the finding that Feed-Forward Network (FFN) in language models can act as “key-value memory”, we propose <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">U</span>ncertainty-<span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">a</span>ware <span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">O</span>bservation <span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">R</span>einjection (<span id="abstract1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>), an effective, training-free and plug-and-play module for VLA models. Specifically, when the current language model layer exhibits high uncertainty, measured by <em id="abstract1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Action Entropy</em>, it reinjects key observation information into the next layer’s Feed-Forward Network (FFN) through attention retrieval. This mechanism helps VLAs better attend to observations during inference, enabling more confident and faithful action generation. Comprehensive experiments show that our method consistently improves diverse VLA models across simulation and real-world tasks with minimal overhead. Notably, <span id="abstract1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> eliminates the need for additional observation cues or modules, making it a versatile and practical plug-in for existing VLA pipelines. The project page is at <a href="https://uaor.jiabingyang.cn" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://uaor.jiabingyang.cn</a>.</p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6>Machine Learning, ICML
</div><span id="id3" class="ltx_note ltx_role_affiliationnotice"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">affiliationnotice: </span><span id="id3.1" class="ltx_ERROR undefined">\correspondingauthor</span></span></span></span>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recent advancements in Vision–Language Models (VLMs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karamcheti et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Beyer et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> have delivered remarkable capabilities in multimodal understanding and generalization. Building on these foundations, Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> fine-tuned on large-scale robotic datasets integrate visual observations with language instructions to synthesize low-level control actions, exhibiting strong task execution and robust generalization across diverse robotic manipulation scenarios. Despite these strengths, persistent data-collection bottlenecks and considerable training budgets remain key barriers to scaling and deploying VLA models in practice.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To achieve performance gains, many efforts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bhat et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> have explored interventions at the input level, such as augmenting observations with additional observation priors.
TraceVLA  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite> introduces visual trace prompting and fine-tunes on 150K robot manipulation trajectories with visual traces. SpatialVLA  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> utilizes Ego3D Position Encoding to inject 3D information into the input observations of the visual-language-action model. While effective, such methods often rely on additional observation priors (e.g., visual traces, depth maps), auxiliary modules (e.g., depth/point-cloud encoders) and extensive fine-tuning, rendering them resource-intensive and poorly scalable to larger backbones and datasets. This naturally raises the question: <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Is it possible to boost VLA models in a training-free manner, without requiring supplementary observation cues or auxiliary modules?</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:310.5pt;">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Layer-wise uncertainty of OpenVLA-OFT across four LIBERO task suites. </figure></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To answer this, we begin by recognizing that VLA models inherit strong visual perception and scene understanding from their VLM backbones, which are often underutilized in current designs. Our key intuition is that after ingesting the observation, the model tends to progressively “<span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">forget</span>” during forward inference. In other words, observation information, comprising visual input and proprioceptive state (if available) in our setup, fades as network depth increases, akin to human working-memory decay <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ballard et al., 1995</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Horowitz and Wolfe, 1998</a>)</cite>.
<span id="S1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This decay may lead to increased uncertainty: Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reveals an observable rise and sustained high level of uncertainty in the early layers (layers 2-8), a pattern that highly correlates with unfaithful actions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Valle et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. Consistently, Figure <a href="#S1.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that in this uncertainty-rising phase the attention from action tokens to observation tokens drops sharply and then remains at a very low level, indicating that the model rarely consults the observation when predicting actions, and empirically supporting our intuition.</span>
Therefore, a natural idea is to reinforce observation information when model exhibits high uncertainty. Inspired by findings that FFNs can act as key-value memory <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Geva et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jie et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zou et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, we adopt the FFN mechanism to extract key features from observation inputs and reinject them into hidden representations, helping the model maintain clear observation throughout inference.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Building on these insights, we propose a lightweight and effective training-free module, <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">U</span>ncertainty-<span id="S1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">a</span>ware <span id="S1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">O</span>bservation <span id="S1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">R</span>einjection (<span id="S1.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>), for VLA models. It computes layer-wise uncertainty via <em id="S1.p4.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Action Entropy</em>, and reinjects observation features into the FFN of the subsequent layer when the uncertainty exceeds a threshold. This blending mechanism reinforces observation information in high-uncertainty regions.
Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world environments show that <span id="S1.p4.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> consistently improves heterogeneous models across diverse manipulation tasks and embodiments, without retraining or architectural changes. Real-world robotic experiments further validate its practicality and effectiveness.
In summary, our main contributions are as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:10pt;">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <em id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Action Entropy</em>, a tailored metric to quantify layer-wise uncertainty in VLA models. It reveals a mild rise in uncertainty during the early stages of inference, which we attribute to the model’s gradual forgetting of observation information.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present <span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>, a training-free and plug-and-play module that treats FFN layers as “key-value memory” and reinjects observation features into them when model exhibits high uncertainty, reinforcing the model’s attention to observation throughout the inference process.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide rigorous theoretical analysis showing that <span id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> enhances the mutual information between hidden states and observation, reduces information bottleneck loss, and lowers expected conditional entropy to mitigate action uncertainty.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Comprehensive experiments in multiple simulation and real-world environments show that <span id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> yields consistent performance gains across various VLA models without relying on extra observation cues or auxiliary modules, while incurring negligible inference overhead.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Vision-Language-Action Models.</span> Integrating multimodal understanding with action execution, Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models pave the way for more capable robotic systems. A prominent line of works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brohan et al., 2022</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>; <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>)</cite> fine-tune pretrained VLMs on large-scale robot data. RT-2X <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zitkovich et al., 2023</a>)</cite> trains a 55B model on the Open X Embodiment (OXE) dataset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vuong et al., 2023</a>)</cite> while OpenVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> trains a 7B model based on Prismatic <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karamcheti et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> fine-tunes PaliGemma VLM  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Beyer et al., 2024</a>)</cite> with a novel flow matching action head. Another line of works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ye et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bu et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>)</cite> utilize web-scale videos; e.g., UniVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> distills latent actions from internet videos, and EC-Flow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>)</cite> predicts embodiment-centric flow from unlabeled videos. Recent dual-system architectures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Han et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bu et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bjorck et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cui et al., 2025</a>)</cite> separate high-level reasoning (System 2) from low-level control (System 1), showing great promise for scalable general-purpose robotic intelligence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uncertainty in Language Models.</span> Uncertainty in language models typically reflects the ambiguity and reliability of the predictive distribution. A key indicator is <span id="S2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Entropy</span>, where higher values imply lower confidence and potential distribution shift <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ling et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.
Dropout Decoding <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> applies uncertainty-guided token dropout principle to input visual tokens for reliability and quality. Recent study of reinforcement learning for LLMs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> indicates that a minority of high-entropy tokens drives most of the reasoning gains. In the VLA community,  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Valle et al. (2025)</a></cite> propose Token-Based Entropy (TB-E) as one of the uncertainty metrics for VLA models, and  <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karli et al. (2025)</a></cite> leverages token-level uncertainty to enable uncertainty-aware human intervention during robotic manipulation. In our design, we quantify the uncertainty through action entropy to evaluate how well the task is executed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Visual Augmentation for Manipulation.</span> Visual augmentation has emerged as a promising strategy to strengthen perception and enhance reliability in robotic control.
TraceVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite> proposes visual trace prompting to enhance spatial-temporal awareness for generalist robotic policies. PointVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> and 3D-CAVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bhat et al., 2025</a>)</cite> integrate point clouds and depth maps to improve spatial
reasoning capability, respectively. Evo-0<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin et al., 2025</a>)</cite> implicitly injects 3D geometry priors from VGGT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> into VLA models. AimBot <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dai et al., 2025</a>)</cite> overlays shooting lines and scope reticles onto multi-view RGB images to offer auxiliary visual guidance. Compared with these methods, <span id="S2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> augments observations via the model’s inherent FFN layers, without introducing additional visual cues or auxiliary modules.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Methodology</h2>

<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18020v1/uaor_pipeline.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:410/230;" width="410" height="230" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Overall framework of <span id="S3.F3.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span><span id="S3.F3.5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">. We compute action entropy at layer <math id="S3.F3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> to estimate uncertainty. If it exceeds a threshold <math id="S3.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, we reinject observation features, including visual and proprioceptive features (if available), into the next layer’s FFN via a key-value retrieval mechanism, where the input hidden states serve as queries and the observation features act as key-value memory.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Preliminary: Reformulation of FFN</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A typical Feed-Forward Network (FFN) in transformer-based models comprises two fully connected layers with an activation in between. Suppose the input hidden states of FFN are <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> is the sequence length and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> is the hidden dimension, the FFN can be formulated as:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{FFN}(\bm{h})=\phi(\bm{h}\bm{W}_{1})\bm{W}_{2}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>FFN</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒉</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝒉</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{FFN}(\bm{h})=\phi(\bm{h}\bm{W}_{1})\bm{W}_{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> is the activation function like ReLU or SiLU, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{W}_{1}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times D}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{W}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{W}_{2}\in\mathbb{R}^{D\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> are the weight matrices of the two FC layers, typically <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=4d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=4d</annotation></semantics></math>.
Note that <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{W}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{W}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{W}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{W}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> can be rewritten as follows:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{W}_{1}=(\bm{k}_{1},\bm{k}_{2},...,\bm{k}_{D}),\bm{W}_{2}=(\bm{v}_{1},\bm{v}_{2},...,\bm{v}_{D})^{\top}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒌</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒌</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒌</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑾</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{W}_{1}=(\bm{k}_{1},\bm{k}_{2},...,\bm{k}_{D}),\bm{W}_{2}=(\bm{v}_{1},\bm{v}_{2},...,\bm{v}_{D})^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{k}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒌</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{k}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{v}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{v}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> denote key and value entries, respectively. Then, the FFN can be reformulated as</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{FFN}(\bm{h})=\sum^{D}_{i=1}\phi(\langle\bm{h},\bm{k}_{i}\rangle)\cdot\bm{v}_{i}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>FFN</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝒉</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>D</mi></munderover><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒌</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝒗</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{FFN}(\bm{h})=\sum^{D}_{i=1}\phi(\langle\bm{h},\bm{k}_{i}\rangle)\cdot\bm{v}_{i}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Therefore, the FFN can be viewed as performing a token-wise key-value lookup mechanism, where each token’s hidden state of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒉</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}</annotation></semantics></math> serves as the query to calculate its similarity with keys, and gathering values based on the similarity. This formulation closely resembles a key-value memory storing factual knowledge, as suggested in prior work <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Geva et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jie et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zou et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Problem Formulation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Vision–Language–Action (VLA) models are designed to jointly process observations and language instructions for the purpose of generating appropriate actions for robots. Formally, given the observation <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> at time <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and language instruction <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, a model <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝝅</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> predicts a temporal action sequence <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\bm{a}_{t},\bm{a}_{t+1},...,\bm{a}_{t+H-1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\bm{a}_{t},\bm{a}_{t+1},...,\bm{a}_{t+H-1})</annotation></semantics></math> (i.e., action chunk size <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>) for task execution:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\pi}:(\bm{o}_{t},\bm{l})\rightarrow(\bm{a}_{t},\bm{a}_{t+1},...,\bm{a}_{t+H-1})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝝅</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>𝒍</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\pi}:(\bm{o}_{t},\bm{l})\rightarrow(\bm{a}_{t},\bm{a}_{t+1},...,\bm{a}_{t+H-1}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">In some VLA models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, the observation <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> includes visual input <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}^{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}^{v}</annotation></semantics></math> and proprioceptive state <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}^{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}^{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, concatenated as <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}=[\bm{o}_{t}^{v};\bm{o}_{t}^{p}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup><mo>;</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>p</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}=[\bm{o}_{t}^{v};\bm{o}_{t}^{p}]</annotation></semantics></math>. In other models, the observation considers only the visual modality, i.e., <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}=\bm{o}_{t}^{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>v</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}=\bm{o}_{t}^{v}</annotation></semantics></math>. While in general <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{a}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{a}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> can represent diverse control schemes and end-effector types, we adopt a simplified setup in this work where actions are defined as 7-DoF vectors corresponding to the gripper’s end-effector pose:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{a}_{t}=[\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta z,\Delta\phi,\Delta\theta,\Delta\psi,g]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝒂</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ψ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{a}_{t}=[\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta z,\Delta\phi,\Delta\theta,\Delta\psi,g],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta z</annotation></semantics></math> represent the relative position of the end effector, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\phi,\Delta\theta,\Delta\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ψ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\phi,\Delta\theta,\Delta\psi</annotation></semantics></math> denote the rotation changes, and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates the gripper’s open/close state.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uncertainty measured by <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Action Entropy</em>.</span> Recognizing the central role of entropy as a widely adopted measure of uncertainty, we introduce <em id="S3.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Action Entropy</em>, a VLA-specific metric that quantifies uncertainty via the entropy of action-related output distributions. Note that current VLA models typically follow two architectures: single-system and dual-system.
For single-system models (e.g., OpenVLA-OFT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>), actions are derived directly from hidden states, either as discrete tokens (256-bin discretization using rare vocabulary tokens) or continuous vectors (via MLP or diffusion heads). We compute entropy directly over the action tokens.
For dual-system models (e.g., CogACT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>), System 1 generates actions conditioned on System 2 outputs. We therefore compute entropy over these condition tokens, which guide action generation.
Based on this setup, we define layer-wise action entropy at each time step as:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}^{(\ell)}_{t,n}=-\,\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{K}p^{(\ell)}_{t,n,i}\,\log p^{(\ell)}_{t,n,i}}{\log K}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}^{(\ell)}_{t,n}=-\,\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{K}p^{(\ell)}_{t,n,i}\,\log p^{(\ell)}_{t,n,i}}{\log K},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{p}^{(\ell)}_{t,n}=\{p^{(\ell)}_{t,n,i}\}_{i=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒑</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{p}^{(\ell)}_{t,n}=\{p^{(\ell)}_{t,n,i}\}_{i=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the categorical probability distribution over top-<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> candidate tokens for the <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-th action or condition token, obtained by projecting the FFN outputs at layer <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> through the <span id="S3.SS3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">language modeling head (LM Head) and normalizing with softmax, which is a standard practice in the "Logit Lens" paradigm <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">nostalgebraist, 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">Belrose et al., 2023</a>)</cite></span>. For discrete actions, we set <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=256</annotation></semantics></math> to match the number of action bins, since the model tends to assign higher probability mass to these 256 action tokens. For continuous actions, we likewise fix <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=256</annotation></semantics></math> for definitional convenience and cross-setting consistency.
Based on this formulation, we define the uncertainty of each layer as the average action entropy over all action tokens or condition tokens:</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}^{(\ell)}\;=\;\frac{1}{N_{a}}\sum_{n=1}^{N_{a}}\mathcal{H}^{(\ell)}_{t,n}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></munderover><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}^{(\ell)}\;=\;\frac{1}{N_{a}}\sum_{n=1}^{N_{a}}\mathcal{H}^{(\ell)}_{t,n},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of selected tokens (see Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Baselines and Setup ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a> for model-specific settings).
Eq. <a href="#S3.E7" title="Equation 7 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows that higher action entropy indicates greater uncertainty. This formulation enables tracking uncertainty dynamics across layers. Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> visualizes these trends for OpenVLA-OFT across four task suites. We observe a slight increase in uncertainty during the early layers of inference.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection (<span id="alg1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>) for VLA Models</figcaption>

            VLA model <math id="alg1.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝝅</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>, observation <math id="alg1.l1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, language instruction <math id="alg1.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒍</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{l}</annotation></semantics></math>

              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">2:</span></span>
              
              
            Action tokens <math id="alg1.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{y}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{y}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> at time step <math id="alg1.l2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
              
              
            <span id="alg1.l3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">At time step <math id="alg1.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>:</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">4:</span></span>

<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Observation Reinjection with FFN.</span> As previously discussed, early layers often exhibit high uncertainty, a pattern highly correlated with the decay of observation attention. To mitigate this, we introduce <span id="S3.SS3.p2.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection</span> (<span id="S3.SS3.p2.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>), illustrated in Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
Specifically, during the forward pass, we compute the uncertainty <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}^{(\ell)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}^{(\ell)}</annotation></semantics></math> based on the action entropy at the current layer <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>. If this uncertainty exceeds a chosen threshold <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, it indicates that the model requires clearer observation guidance. Since the forward pass for layer <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> is completed, we perform reinjection at the <span id="S3.SS3.p2.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">subsequent</span> layer (<math id="S3.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math>) to avoid the computational and memory overhead associated with backtracking.
Concretely, we treat the encoded observation features as a key-value memory. We use the hidden states entering the FFN at layer <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted as <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math>, as queries to attend over this memory. The retrieved features are then blended with the original output of the FFN at layer <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math>. The formulated process is defined as:</p>
<table id="S3.E8" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E8X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\operatorname{FFN}^{(\ell+1)}\!\left(\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\bm{o}_{t}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>FFN</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\operatorname{FFN}^{(\ell+1)}\!\left(\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\bm{o}_{t}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\alpha\,\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\!\left(\bm{o}_{t}\mid\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\alpha\,\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\!\left(\bm{o}_{t}\mid\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E8Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E8Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle+(1-\alpha)\,\operatorname{FFN}^{(\ell+1)}\!\left(\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.337em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msup><mi>FFN</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle+(1-\alpha)\,\operatorname{FFN}^{(\ell+1)}\!\left(\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> is the blending ratio. The retrieved observation features <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> are computed using <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> as the queries:</p>
<table id="S3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\bm{o}_{t}\mid\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})=\sum_{i=1}^{N_{o}}\phi(\langle\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\bm{o}_{t,i}\rangle)\cdot\bm{o}_{t,i}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></munderover><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝒉</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\bm{o}_{t}\mid\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})=\sum_{i=1}^{N_{o}}\phi(\langle\bm{h}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\bm{o}_{t,i}\rangle)\cdot\bm{o}_{t,i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}=(\bm{o}_{t,1},...,\bm{o}_{t,N_{o}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}=(\bm{o}_{t,1},...,\bm{o}_{t,N_{o}})</annotation></semantics></math> serves as the key-value memory. This design allows the model to dynamically "re-attend" to the observation in the next layer when confusion arises, without needing to halt or backtrack the inference. The complete algorithmic flow is detailed in Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Theoretical Analysis: Why <span id="S3.SS4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> Works</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To understand the effectiveness of <span id="S3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>, we provide a theoretical analysis grounded in the following four theorems:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Notation.</span> At time step <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and layer <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> be the vanilla FFN output, <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> the output after applying <span id="S3.SS4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> (Eq. <a href="#S3.E8" title="Equation 8 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>), and <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> the reinjected observation features (Eq. <a href="#S3.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). Let <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the observation, <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{y}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{y}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> the action tokens, and <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> the full input (observation + language).</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Observation information gain)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If reinjection is non-degenerate and mixing is near-invertible, then <span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> increases the mutual information between the hidden state and observation:</span></p>
<table id="S3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\!\left(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\right)\;\geq\;I\!\left(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.280em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">≥</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\!\left(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\right)\;\geq\;I\!\left(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">with strict inequality if <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> adds observation-dependent variability.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Action uncertainty reduction)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assuming a deterministic backbone and stochastic policy head, the conditional entropy over actions is reduced if Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Observation information gain). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> holds:</span></p>
<table id="S3.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.3</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Information Bottleneck optimization)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(r)=I(r;\bm{x}_{t})-\beta I(r;\bm{y}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(r)=I(r;\bm{x}_{t})-\beta I(r;\bm{y}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> be the Information Bottleneck (IB) objective. Then <span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> optimizes IB when:</span></p>
<table id="S3.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})\leq\mathcal{L}(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})\quad\text{if}\quad\Delta stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>β</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation <td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta I_{t,y}^{(\ell+1)}\triangleq I(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{y}_{t})-I(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{y}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta I_{t,y}^{(\ell+1)}\triangleq I(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{y}_{t})-I(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{y}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta I_{t,x}^{(\ell+1)}\triangleq I(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{x}_{t})-I(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{x}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover I_{t,x}^{(\ell+1)}\triangleq I(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{x}_{t})-I(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{x}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.4</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Benefit of uncertainty-triggered reinjection)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If the entropy-based layer uncertainty <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}^{(\ell)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}^{(\ell)}</annotation></semantics></math> correlates positively with <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐲</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})</annotation></semantics></math>, then conditioning reinjection on <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}^{(\ell)}&gt;\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}^{(\ell)}&gt;\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> increases the expected relevance of injected information:</span></p>
<table id="S3.E13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
