<div id="S3.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Theoretical Integration.</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> Proofs are provided in Appendix </span><a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Proofs for Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. These four theorems form a </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">unified logical framework</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> explaining why </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">UaOR</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> works:
Theorem </span><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Observation information gain). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> establishes the </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">mechanism</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, guaranteeing that reinjection restores observation information.
Theorem </span><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Action uncertainty reduction). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> links this to the </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">effect</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, proving that this information gain mathematically precipitates a reduction in action uncertainty.
Theorem </span><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3.3 (Information Bottleneck optimization). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.14" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> justifies the </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">objective</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.16" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> via the Information Bottleneck principle, ensuring that the reinjection contributes valid predictive cues rather than mere noise or redundancy.
Finally, Theorem </span><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 3.4 (Benefit of uncertainty-triggered reinjection). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.17" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> validates our </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.18" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">control strategy</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.19" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, confirming that entropy-based triggering maximizes the expected relevance of the injected information compared to indiscriminate injection.
Together, they theoretically ground </span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.20" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">UaOR</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.21" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> as a method that optimizes model confidence through targeted and efficient information restoration.</span><span id="S3.SS4.p3.1.22" class="ltx_text"></span></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Simulation Experiments</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Simulation Benchmarks and Baselines.</span>
We conduct evaluations on three widely-used simulation benchmarks in robot learning: LIBERO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, SIMPLER <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025d</a>)</cite>, and CALVIN <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mees et al., 2022</a>)</cite>.
For these benchmarks, we select several representative VLA models as our baseline: OpenVLA-OFT (7B) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> (3B) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>)</cite></span> for LIBERO, CogACT (7B) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> for SIMPLER, and LLaVA-VLA (0.5B) for CALVIN.
These baselines differ in both architecture and scale—OpenVLA-OFT and LLaVA-VLA are single-system models, while <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and CogACT follow dual-system design; model sizes range from 0.5B to 7B parameters.
This setup enables a comprehensive assessment of <span id="S4.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>’s impact across heterogeneous VLA models, tasks, and embodiments. The main experiments are conducted on NVIDIA 4090 GPUs under three different random seeds to ensure consistency and reliability. It is worth noting that our reproduction uses the official checkpoints, and results may vary slightly due to the specific model weights and hardware resources.
More implementation details are presented in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>

</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Experimental Results on LIBERO.<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Based on OpenVLA-OFT, <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> delivers consistent gains across all four suites and achieves a remarkable average success rate of </span>98.0%<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">, as shown in Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. Notably, this performance is comparable to the recent 3D-CAVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bhat et al., 2025</a>)</cite> (</span>98.1%<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">), yet <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> eliminates the need for auxiliary depth inputs, CoT reasoning, and fine-tuning, demonstrating superior efficiency. Validating generality, <span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> also consistently boosts the cutting-edge dual-system policy <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>)</cite> by </span>+1.5<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> points on average. The pronounced gains on </span>LIBERO-Long<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> across both architectures (</span>+2.0<span id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">) suggest that selectively reinforcing observation information effectively mitigates the “forgetting” of perceptual cues and reduces error accumulation during complex sequential reasoning.</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experimental Results on SIMPLER.</span>
Table <a href="#S4.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> raises the average success rate of CogACT by <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+2.6</span> points (73.1 <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> 75.7; <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3.6%</span> relative). The improvements are most evident on <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Pick coke can</span> (<span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+2.7</span>), <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Open top drawer and place apple</span> (both <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+3.7</span>) and <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Move near</span> (<span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+3.4</span>), with a smaller gain on <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Open/Close drawer</span> (+0.9). These tasks demand precise localization and placement under visual clutter, and the results suggest that uncertainty-aware observation reinjection improves scene grounding and decision reliability <em id="S4.SS1.p3.1.12" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">without</em> extra priors or retraining, validating the utility of <span id="S4.SS1.p3.1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> as a training-free plug-in module.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Experimental Results on CALVIN.</span>
As demonstrated in Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.1 Simulation Experiments ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, with LLaVA-VLA on the ABC<math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>D split (Fig. 3), <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> improves success on every track and increases the average consecutive completion length by <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+0.12</span> (3.55 <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> 3.67; <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">3.4%</span> relative). The consistent gains across progressively longer task chains indicate better maintenance of observation fidelity leading to reduced uncertainty in downstream action prediction. Together with LIBERO and SIMPLER, these results substantiate that <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> provides reliable, training-free improvements across heterogeneous VLA architectures, tasks, and embodiments.
We also provide additional experimental results in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C More Experimental Results ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>, including multi-seed evaluations and qualitative visualizations to further show the effectiveness of <span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Real-World Experiments</h3>

<figure id="S4.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18020v1/real_robot.png" id="S4.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/250;" width="476" height="250" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S4.F4.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Real-World Setup and Results.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Real-World Setup.</span> We perform real-robot experiments to validate the effectiveness of <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> in the real world. Our real-robot setup includes a Franka Research 3 robot arm equipped with a parallel-jaw gripper, a static ZED 2i camera, and a 3D mouse (Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Real-World Experiments ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). In total, we evaluate on four tasks: 1) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Close the upper drawer</span>, 2) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Put the redbull on the plate</span>, 3) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Put the lion on the top shelf</span>, and 4) <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Stand the coke can up</span>. These tasks range from simple short-horizon placement to complex long-horizon multi-stage manipulation. <span id="S4.SS2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">We fine-tune both OpenVLA-OFT and CogACT on each task using 50 expert trajectories and evaluate each task with 20 test rollouts (see Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Real-World Setup ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a> for more details).</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Results.</span> Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Real-World Experiments ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> reports the real-world evaluation results on both OpenVLA-OFT and CogACT.
For <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OpenVLA-OFT</span>, we observe consistent performance improvements across <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">all four tasks</span>, with the average success rate increasing from 55.0% to 72.5% (<span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+31.8%</span> relative). The largest relative gain appears on the most challenging task, <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Stand the coke can up</span> (<span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+44.4%</span> relative).
<span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Crucially, <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> demonstrates strong generalizability when applied to <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CogACT</span>. It achieves improvements across <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">all</span> four tasks, boosting the average success rate from 63.8% to 78.8% (<span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">+23.5%</span> relative). Notably, in the <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Put the redbull on the plate</span> task, <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> increases the success rate by an absolute <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">20%</span>. These combined results validate the effectiveness of <span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.7.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> in enhancing manipulation robustness and generating faithful actions across different model architectures in real-world scenarios.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Ablation Studies</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we conduct ablation studies on the LIBERO benchmark based on OpenVLA-OFT to investigate the effectiveness of our design choices.</p>

<tr id="S4.T4.5.1.10" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> (Random)</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">Attn</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_r" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">Random</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">97.8</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">97.6</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">96.4</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">93.6</td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.10.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;">96.4</td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T4.5.1.11" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.11.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">UaOR<span id="S4.T4.5.1.11.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright"> (Ours)</span></span></td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.11.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.11.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">Attn</span></td>

<td id="S4.T4.5.1.11.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.11.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">99.0</span></td>
<td id="S4.T4.5.1.11.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.11.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">98.4</span></td>

<td id="S4.T4.5.1.11.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:2.3pt;padding-right:2.3pt;"><span id="S4.T4.5.1.11.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">98.0</span></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Ablation on Core Designs.<span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> presents a factorial ablation on injection mechanisms, feature extraction (Feat.), and trigger policies (Trig.). We define <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Mean-Residual</span> as directly adding mean-pooled observation features to the FFN’s output hidden states and <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Mean-Blending</span> as <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>-blending. Trigger policies include <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">All Layers</span>, <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Random</span> (matching the injection rate of Entropy-based), and <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Entropy-based</span> (uncertainty threshold). More details are in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS4" title="B.4 Ablation on Core Designs ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>.
Results reveal three insights:
(1) </span>Injection Mechanism:<span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Direct addition causes catastrophic collapse (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>) due to severe feature shifts, whereas <math id="S4.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>-blending ensures stability. <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Mean-Residual</span> (Random) survives (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.9\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">96.9</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.9\%</annotation></semantics></math>) only because its sparsity allows model recovery in subsequent layers.
(2) </span>Feature Extraction:<span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Even with stable blending, Mean Pooling (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">96.3</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.2\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">97.2</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.2\%</annotation></semantics></math>) struggles to surpass the strong baseline (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">97.1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>). This is because averaging assigns equal weight to all observation tokens, failing to distinguish relevant cues. In contrast, <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>’s Attentive Retrieval succeeds by effectively extracting fine-grained context relevant to the current hidden state.
(3) </span>Trigger Policy:<span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> For <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>, indiscriminate injection (<span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">All/Random Layers</span>) acts as noise, degrading performance (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.7\%/96.4\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">96.7</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">/</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">96.4</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.7\%/96.4\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Only entropy-based triggering yields improvements (<math id="S4.SS3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">98.0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Additionally, we have also performed an ablation study in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 Ablation on Injection Timing and Location ‣ Appendix C More Experimental Results ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a> to empirically verify the necessity and efficiency of injecting into the next layer’s FFN compared to other architectural alternatives. Collectively, these findings validate the effectiveness of the core designs of <span id="S4.SS3.p2.1.1.4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>.</span></span></p>
</div>

</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Why Select Observation to Reinject?</span>
Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> presents an ablation on the type of information reinjected into FFN layers. Results show that reinjecting observation information (i.e., visual and proprioceptive features) yields the most consistent performance improvements. In contrast, reinjecting instruction features—either alone or in combination—leads to no improvement or even performance drops. This suggests that visual and proprioceptive features play a critical role in guiding robot behavior, while also revealing a potential limitation of current VLA models—their insufficient instruction-following capability and tendency to overfit to static language inputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The Impact of <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>.</span>
Figure <a href="#S4.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> illustrates the effect of varying the uncertainty threshold <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and the blending factor <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> on the performance of OpenVLA-OFT with <span id="S4.SS3.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>.
Figures <a href="#S4.F5.sf1" title="Figure 5(a) ‣ Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5(a)</span></a> and  <a href="#S4.F5.sf2" title="Figure 5(b) ‣ Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5(b)</span></a> show the marginal effects when fixing one hyperparameter to its optimal value.
<span id="S4.SS3.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">To further investigate their interaction, we present a joint sensitivity analysis on LIBERO-Long in Figure <a href="#S4.F5.sf3" title="Figure 5(c) ‣ Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5(c)</span></a>.
As demonstrated by the 3D surface plot, the performance follows a convex trend, indicating that <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> must be balanced to achieve optimal results.
Specifically, we observe two failure modes at the extremes:
(1) <span id="S4.SS3.p4.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Over-correction</span>: A small <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> (frequent injection) coupled with a large <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> (strong mixing) degrades performance, likely by disrupting critical internal representations.
(2) <span id="S4.SS3.p4.1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Under-correction</span>: A large <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> (rare injection) coupled with a small <math id="S4.SS3.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> (weak mixing) fails to provide sufficient observation guidance.
The distinct peak in Figure <a href="#S4.F5.sf3" title="Figure 5(c) ‣ Figure 5 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5(c)</span></a> confirms our selected parameters lie within the optimal region. In practice, we use an efficient heuristic strategy detailed in Appendix <a href="#A2.SS2" title="B.2 Baselines and Setup ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.2</span></a> to determine these values.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F5" class="ltx_figure ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F5.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 5</span>: </span><span id="S4.F5.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Impact of uncertainty threshold <math id="S4.F5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> and blending factor <math id="S4.F5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> across four LIBERO task suites.</span></figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">

<div id="S4.SS3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Complexity Analysis.</span>
Although <span id="S4.SS3.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> proves highly effective, an important consideration is its computational cost. To this end, we conduct a theoretical complexity analysis on it (which can be found in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Theoretical Complexity Analysis ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>) and test the actual runtime overhead through empirical experiments. Specifically, we run 500 rollouts on the LIBERO-Long benchmark using OpenVLA-OFT. As shown in Table <a href="#S4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 4.3 Ablation Studies ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, applying <span id="S4.SS3.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> results in only a slight throughput drop from 49.7 Hz to 47.3 Hz (-4.8%), and a marginal latency increase from 0.161s to 0.169s (+5.0%). These results indicate that <span id="S4.SS3.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> introduces negligible computational overhead in practice.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present <span id="S5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>, a lightweight, training-free module designed to boost VLA models. By introducing action entropy as a measure of inference-time uncertainty, <span id="S5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> dynamically reinjects observation information into the next-layer FFN when uncertainty is high, allowing the model to refocus on silent observation features and leading to more confident and reliable action generation. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating its efficiency, and validate its effectiveness across a wide range of VLA models, tasks, and embodiments in both simulation and real-world experiments. Without requiring additional observation cues, modules or training, <span id="S5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> consistently achieves performance gains with negligible computational overhead, making it an effective and plug-and-play module for existing VLA models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Impact Statements</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This work aims to contribute to the advancement of Embodied Intelligence. While our research may have various potential societal implications, none of which we feel must be specifically highlighted here.</p>
</div>
</section>

<span class="ltx_bibblock"><span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_author">B. Zitkovich, T. Yu, S. Xu, P. Xu, T. Xiao, F. Xia, J. Wu, P. Wohlhart, S. Welker, A. Wahid, <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_etal">et al.</span></span>

<section id="Ax1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Appendix</h2>

</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Proofs for Theoretical Analysis: Why <span id="A1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> Works</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we provide rigorous proofs for the four theorems stated in Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>, grounded in the Information Bottleneck (IB) theory.
We show that <span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> increases the Mutual Information (MI) between hidden states and the observation memory, thereby reducing the conditional entropy given the hidden states, and further improving the Information Bottleneck (IB) objective.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Preliminaries.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At time step <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and layer <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell{+}1</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> be the vanilla FFN output, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> the output after applying <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> (Eq. <a href="#S3.E8" title="Equation 8 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>), and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> the retrieved observation information (Eq. <a href="#S3.E9" title="Equation 9 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). Let <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> be the observation memory, <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{y}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{y}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> the action tokens, and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> the full input (observation + language). We write
<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\triangleq\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\,\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>≜</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\triangleq\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\,\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}=g\!\big(T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.343em;" width="0.343em"><mi>g</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}=g\!\big(T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)</annotation></semantics></math> for the <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> fusion function induced by Eq. <a href="#S3.E8" title="Equation 8 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.
We assume:</p>
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.4em;">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(A1) <span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Non-degenerate reinjection:</span> <math id="A1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\!\big(\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\!\big(\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> on a set of non-zero measure.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(A2) <span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Near-invertible mixing:</span> <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> admits an approximate left inverse <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}\|\psi(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})-T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}\|\psi(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})-T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\|_{2}^{2}\leq\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, implying a strong-DPI type bound <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">Raginsky, 2016</a>; <a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">Polyanskiy and Wu, 2016</a>; <a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2005</a>)</cite></p>
<table id="A1.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">for any <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> jointly distributed with <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\eta_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\!\to\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>κ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>η</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\eta_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\!\to\!0</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A1.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\!\to\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\!\to\!0</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., Fano/Gaussian bounds).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(A3) <span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Target generation:</span> <math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{y}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{y}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is generated from <math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> through the policy head; conditioned on <math id="A1.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{x}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒙</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{x}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, the rest of the network is deterministic (standard in IB-style analyses <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tishby et al., 2000</a>; <a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">Alemi et al., 2017</a>)</cite>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma A.1</span></span><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Layerwise MI decay in the vanilla stack)<span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A1.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)\leq I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐨</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐡</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐨</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)\leq I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)};\bm{o}_{t}\big).</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Each layer computes <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}=f^{(\ell+1)}\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}=f^{(\ell+1)}\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)}\big)</annotation></semantics></math> with no direct access to <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, so
<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{o}_{t}\!\to\!\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)}\!\to\!\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{o}_{t}\!\to\!\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)}\!\to\!\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> is a Markov chain. According to the <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Data Processing Inequality (DPI)</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cover et al., 1991</a>)</cite>, if A → B → C forms a Markov chain, then: <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A;C)\leq I(A;B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A;C)\leq I(A;B)</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus we can get
<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)\leq I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)\leq I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell)};\bm{o}_{t}\big).</annotation></semantics></math>
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Observation information gain). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a></span> (Observation information gain).
At layer <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell{+}1</annotation></semantics></math> and time <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, augment by <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}=\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{t}^{(\ell+1)}=\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)},\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)</annotation></semantics></math>. By the chain rule,</p>

<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Letting <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> proves
<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\!\big(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)\geq I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\!\big(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big)\geq I\!\big(\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\big),</annotation></semantics></math>
with strict inequality when <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I\!\big(\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.348em;" width="0.348em"><mi>I</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>;</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I\!\big(\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Action uncertainty reduction). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a></span> (Action uncertainty reduction).

<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.5" class="ltx_p">Letting <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon\!\to\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon\!\to\!0</annotation></semantics></math> proves
<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})\leq H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})\leq H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})</annotation></semantics></math>,
with strict inequality whenever
<math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\bm{y}_{t};\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>;</mo><msubsup><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\bm{y}_{t};\textsc{inj}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3.3 (Information Bottleneck optimization). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a></span> (Information Bottleneck improvement).

stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><mover stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>provided</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" I_{t,y\mid\tilde{h}}^{\ell+1,\min}&gt;\eta_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\varepsilon).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.8" class="ltx_p">When <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficiently small (so that <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\varepsilon),\eta_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\varepsilon)\!\to\!0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>κ</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>η</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ε</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\varepsilon),\eta_{t}^{(\ell+1)}(\varepsilon)\!\to\!0</annotation></semantics></math>), the sufficient condition Eq. <a href="#A1.E16" title="Equation 16 ‣ Preliminaries. ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> simplifies to</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.9" class="ltx_p">This condition provides a lower bound for <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> to ensure that reinjecting observation information at layer <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math> reduces the IB objective for VLA models. Satisfying this criterion allows <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p6.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> to effectively optimize the trade-off between compressing task-irrelevant input and retaining observation-relevant information critical for accurate action generation.
∎</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 3.4 (Benefit of uncertainty-triggered reinjection). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a></span> (Benefit of uncertainty-triggered reinjection).
Let <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}^{(\ell)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}^{(\ell)}</annotation></semantics></math> be the entropy-based layer uncertainty; assume it is positively correlated with <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)</annotation></semantics></math>. Define the <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">predictive relevance</em> of the injection at layer <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell{+}1</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
