<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)\ \leq\ H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)\ -\ R_{t}^{(\ell+1)}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.500em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.778em">≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.500em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.722em">−</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)\ \leq\ H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\tilde{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)\ -\ R_{t}^{(\ell+1)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.6" class="ltx_p">so triggering on <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{t}^{(\ell)}&gt;\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>u</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{t}^{(\ell)}&gt;\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> yields a larger <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.6.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">expected</em> reduction of <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.742em;" width="0.742em"><mi>H</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H\!\big(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)}\big)</annotation></semantics></math> per reinjection call.
∎</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Summary.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">(A) <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Layerwise forgetting</em> in standard transformer stacks leads to diminishing observation relevance across depth (Lemma <a href="#A1.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma A.1 (Layerwise MI decay in the vanilla stack). ‣ Preliminaries. ‣ Appendix A Proofs for Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.1</span></a>).
(B) <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">recovers</em> observation dependence at layer <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell{+}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell{+}1</annotation></semantics></math>, provably increasing <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝒐</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)};\bm{o}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> over the vanilla baseline (Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 3.1 (Observation information gain). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>), which in turn <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">reduces</em> conditional entropy <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝒚</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝒉</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(\bm{y}_{t}\mid\hat{\bm{h}}_{t}^{(\ell+1)})</annotation></semantics></math> (Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Action uncertainty reduction). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>).
(C) When the relevance gain <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta I_{y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>y</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta I_{y}</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds the scaled compression cost <math id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{\beta}\Delta I_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>β</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>x</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\beta}\Delta I_{x}</annotation></semantics></math>, <span id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">lowers</em> the IB objective, improving the overall information–efficiency tradeoff (Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3.3 (Information Bottleneck optimization). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).
(D) Entropy-based triggering <em id="A1.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">selectively activates</em> reinjection in high-uncertainty regions, thereby increasing the expected predictive value of injected content and enhancing per-call entropy reduction (Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Theorem 3.4 (Benefit of uncertainty-triggered reinjection). ‣ 3.4 Theoretical Analysis: Why UaOR Works ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>More Implementation Details</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Simulation Benchmarks</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LIBERO</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2023</a>)</cite> is a language-conditioned manipulation benchmark that factorizes variation along four axes and evaluates policies under controlled shifts of <em id="A2.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">geometry</em>, <em id="A2.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">object identity</em>, <em id="A2.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">goal intent</em>, and <em id="A2.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">temporal horizon</em>. The benchmark provides 4 suites—<span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Spatial</span>, <span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Object</span>, <span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Goal</span>, and <span id="A2.SS1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Long</span>—each containing 10 tasks with 50 human-teleoperated demonstrations per task, yielding a consistent protocol for training and evaluation. These suites focus on distinct reasoning capabilities:</p>
<ul id="A2.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:10pt;">
<li id="A2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LIBERO Spatial</span> holds objects and goals fixed while perturbing placements and poses, stressing relational language parsing (e.g., left/right, front/behind) and viewpoint robustness.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LIBERO-Object</span> fixes scene layout but varies categories/attributes (type, shape, color), probing category-level generalization and attribute-aware grounding.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LIBERO-Goal</span> keeps geometry and objects constant while changing the intended outcome, testing fine-grained instruction disambiguation and goal-consistent action selection.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LIBERO-Long</span> composes multiple atomic skills into extended procedures across diverse scenes, assessing sequential planning, error recovery, and long-horizon credit assignment.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">SIMPLER</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2025d</a>)</cite> is a simulated evaluation suite designed to mirror real-world manipulation with two complementary settings. <em id="A2.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Visual Matching (VM)</em> aligns the simulated scene with its real counterpart (assets, layout, camera), enabling faithful assessment of policies in near-deployment conditions. <em id="A2.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Variant Aggregations (VA)</em> perturbs the VM setup—varying background, lighting, distractors, and table textures—to stress-test robustness and out-of-distribution generalization.
For the <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Google robot</span>, both VM and VA include four canonical tasks: 1) <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Pick coke can</span>; 2) <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Move near</span>; and 3) <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Open/Close drawer</span>, and 4) <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Open top drawer and place apple</span>.
For the <span id="A2.SS1.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WidowX robot</span>, SIMPLER provides the <em id="A2.SS1.p2.1.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">VM</em> setting with four tasks: 1) Put spoon on towel, 2) Put carrot on plate, 3) Stack green block on yellow block, and 4) Put eggplant in yellow basket.
Evaluation is reported as success rate over standardized rollouts for fair comparison across methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CALVIN</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mees et al., 2022</a>)</cite> is a long-horizon manipulation benchmark built on top of the PyBullet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Coumans and Bai, 2016</a>)</cite> simulator and involves a Franka Panda Robot arm that manipulates the scene. It comprises 34 tasks across four environments (A, B, C, and D) and over six hours of teleoperated play data per environment, captured from static and wrist-mounted RGB-D cameras together with tactile signals and proprioception.
We adopt the classic and challenging CALVIN ABC<math id="A2.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math>D evaluation protocol, where each model is assessed over 500 rollouts. We report both the overall success rate and the average number of successfully completed sub-tasks (i.e., average length).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Baselines and Setup</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we delve into the architectural details of the selected baselines and provide additional information on the experimental setup used throughout our evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OpenVLA-OFT</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> is a high-performance VLA model derived from OpenVLA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>. It incorporates parallel decoding with action chunking, continuous action representation, and an L1 regression objective, leading to substantial improvements in both task performance and inference speed. In our experiments, we use the OpenVLA-OFT variant trained with multimodal inputs consisting of two images (a third-person image and a wrist camera image), the robot’s proprioceptive state, and a language instruction. Specifically, the visual and proprioceptive features are concatenated to form the observation features, which are then injected into the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) layers of the language model following our <span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> mechanism. And we compute the action entropy based on all action tokens within the action chunk. We use the hidden states corresponding to the last <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}=8\times 7=56" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}=8\times 7=56</annotation></semantics></math> (action chunk size <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=8</annotation></semantics></math>, action dimension <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{a}=7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{a}=7</annotation></semantics></math>) tokens (i.e., positions <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[-57:-1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>57</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0em">:</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-57:-1]</annotation></semantics></math>) before the final stop token (“&lt;/s&gt;”) to measure the uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{\pi_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝝅</mi><mn>𝟎</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{\pi_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Black et al., 2024</a>)</cite> employs a flow matching-based architecture built upon the PaliGemma VLM (3B). It processes multimodal inputs (images and language instructions) through the VLM backbone to generate context embeddings (specifically, the Key-Value cache), which then condition a separate action expert for continuous action generation. For the adaptation of our approach, we employ the officially released PyTorch codebase and the corresponding model checkpoints. In our experiments, we inject the visual features into the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) layers of the PaliGemma backbone. Since the flow matching head operates in continuous space and does not output discrete action probabilities, we compute the entropy based on the <span id="A2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">last token</span> of the VLM’s prefix processing (i.e., position <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1]</annotation></semantics></math>). This metric reflects the backbone’s semantic uncertainty regarding the current observation and instruction context before the denoising phase. Consequently, we set <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}=1</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. <a href="#S3.E7" title="Equation 7 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> for this architecture.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CogACT</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> adopts a componentized dual-system architecture that decouples perception and control. It uses the Prismatic VLM (7B) to extract a cognition token, which conditions a diffusion-based action expert for generating precise actions. CogACT demonstrates state-of-the-art results on the SIMPLER benchmark. In our implementation, since CogACT does not utilize proprioceptive input (i.e., robot joint states), we treat only the visual observation (third-person image) as the modality for observation reinjection. Additionally, we compute the action entropy solely based on the generated cognition token (i.e., positions <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1]</annotation></semantics></math>), which serves as the intermediate representation linking perception and action. Therefore, <math id="A2.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}=1</annotation></semantics></math> in Eq. <a href="#S3.E7" title="Equation 7 ‣ 3.3 Uncertainty-Aware Observation Reinjection ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> for this setup.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LLaVA-VLA</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhao et al., 2025b</a>)</cite> is built on the widely adopted vision-language model LLaVA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, exhibiting stable performance across both simulated and real-world environments. The lightweight variant LLaVA-VLA-0.5b achieves performance comparable to its 7B counterpart based on LLaVA, while incurring significantly lower computational overhead. It incorporates two images (static image and gripper image) and proprioception as input, which we combine as the supplemental observation cues. While LLaVA-VLA adopts action chunking, unlike OpenVLA-OFT, it does not employ parallel decoding and thus generates only one action token per step. Therefore we utilize the last token (i.e., positions <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A2.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}=1</annotation></semantics></math>) to compute action entropy and uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">For other baseline methods compared in the main text, we list them for reference and encourage readers to refer to the original papers for further details.</p>
</div>

<tr id="A2.T7.6.1.22" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A2.T7.6.1.22.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="A2.T7.6.1.22.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">Stand the coke can up</span></td>
<td id="A2.T7.6.1.22.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A2.T7.6.1.22.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">0.80</span></td>
<td id="A2.T7.6.1.22.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A2.T7.6.1.22.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:50%;">0.05</span></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A2.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Hyperparameter Selection Strategy.</span>
We adopt a heuristic strategy to determine the hyperparameters <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> (uncertainty threshold) and <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> (blending factor). We begin by analyzing the uncertainty curves (see Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) to obtain a coarse estimate, initially setting <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma=0.80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma=0.80</annotation></semantics></math> for all task suites in LIBERO. Under this preliminary setting, we search for the optimal <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> and find that <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=0.05</annotation></semantics></math> yields the best performance across all four LIBERO task suites. Fixing <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, we then refine <math id="A2.SS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for each individual task by performing a local search around the initial estimate. This progressive narrowing of the search space significantly reduces the tuning overhead while ensuring strong empirical results. We use the strategy to determine the final hyperparameter settings for both simulation and real-world experiments, as summarized in Table <a href="#A2.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ B.2 Baselines and Setup ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="A2.T8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 8</span>: </span><span id="A2.T8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">OpenVLA-OFT hyperparameters for real-world fine-tuning.</span></figcaption>

<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Real-World Setup</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4.2 Real-World Experiments ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> illustrates our real-robot setting. The platform comprises a 7-DoF Franka Research 3 robot arm with a parallel-jaw gripper and a ZED 2i stereo camera mounted on a tripod. We collect expert trajectories with a 3D mouse to enable fine-grained and precise manipulation. The four tasks we designed are detailed as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A2.I2" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:10pt;">
<li id="A2.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Close the upper drawer.</span>
The robot is required to approach the cabinet, locate the upper drawer, and execute a pushing motion to close it fully.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Put the redbull on the plate.</span>
The robot needs to identify the Red Bull can, grasp it securely, and place it on the designated plate area with proper orientation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Put the lion on the top shelf.</span>
The robot should pick up the toy lion from the workspace and accurately place it onto the top shelf.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A2.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A2.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Stand the coke can up.</span> The robot must perform a complex sequence of actions to pick up a horizontally lying cup, reorient it upright, and place it stably on its base.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">We fine-tune both OpenVLA-OFT and CogACT on each task using 50 expert trajectories collected with a 3D spacemouse. The training hyperparameters for OpenVLA-OFT and CogACT are detailed in Table <a href="#A2.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ B.2 Baselines and Setup ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> and Table <a href="#A2.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ B.2 Baselines and Setup ‣ Appendix B More Implementation Details ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, respectively.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span><span id="A2.SS4.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Ablation on Core Designs</span></h3>

<div id="A2.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In this section, we provide more details about the ablation study on the core designs of <span id="A2.SS4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>:</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Mean-Residual:<span id="A2.SS4.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Directly adds the mean-pooled observation features to the hidden state (<math id="A2.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{\prime}=h+o_{mean}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">′</mo></msup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">o</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{\prime}=h+o_{mean}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A2.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is the original FFN’s output hidden states and <math id="A2.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{mean}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">o</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{mean}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the mean-pooled observation features) . Represents a naive residual connection. Since the observation tokens and hidden states differ in sequence length, element-wise addition (standard ResNet) is impossible. Therefore, we aggregate observation features via </span>Mean Pooling<span id="A2.SS4.p2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> for the residual baselines.</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Mean-Blending:<span id="A2.SS4.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Blends the mean-pooled observation features using <math id="A2.SS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A2.SS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{\prime}=(1-\alpha)h+\alpha o_{mean}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">′</mo></msup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">o</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">n</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{\prime}=(1-\alpha)h+\alpha o_{mean}</annotation></semantics></math>). Represents a "softer" residual.</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_smallcaps" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">UaOR<span id="A2.SS4.p4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright">:<span id="A2.SS4.p4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Blends the key observation features relevant to current hidden states via an FFN-like key-value retrieval.</span></span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Trigger Policies:<span id="A2.SS4.p5.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> </span>All Layers (All)<span id="A2.SS4.p5.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> injects observation features at every layer of the LLM backbone. </span>Random Layers (Random)<span id="A2.SS4.p5.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> selects a subset of layers uniformly at random for each inference step. To ensure a fair comparison, the number of selected layers matches the average number of layers triggered by the Entropy-based policy (e.g., approximately 30% for LIBERO-Spatial, Object, and Goal, and 20% for LIBERO-Long). </span>Entropy-based (Entropy)<span id="A2.SS4.p5.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> dynamically triggers injection only at specific layers where the uncertainty measured by action entropy exceeds the threshold <math id="A2.SS4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, targeting moments of high uncertainty.</span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>More Experimental Results</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span><span id="A3.SS1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Ablation on Injection Timing and Location</span></h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">To validate the rationale behind our specific design choices—namely, the “one-layer delay” strategy and the selection of the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) as the injection site—we conduct a detailed ablation study comparing different injection timings and module locations on the LIBERO benchmark based on OpenVLA-OFT. The results are summarized in Table <a href="#A3.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ C.1 Ablation on Injection Timing and Location ‣ Appendix C More Experimental Results ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(1) Why “One-Layer Delay”? (Efficiency &amp; Effectiveness).<span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
We compare injecting into the <span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Current Layer</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>) versus our proposed <span id="A3.SS1.p2.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Next Layer</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math>) strategy.</span></span></p>
<ul id="A3.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:10pt;">
<li id="A3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Effectiveness:<span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> As shown in Table <a href="#A3.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ C.1 Ablation on Injection Timing and Location ‣ Appendix C More Experimental Results ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, injecting into the <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Current FFN</span> (97.7%) and <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Next FFN</span> (98.0%) yields comparable performance. This is because the underlying operation is mathematically identical (using the FFN’s input to retrieve observation features and blending them with the original output). The slight edge for <span id="A3.I1.i1.p1.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Next Layer</span> may stem from using more processed hidden states as the queries.</span></span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Efficiency:<span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Despite similar success rates, the <span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Current Layer</span> strategies incur significantly higher computational overhead. Injecting into the current FFN requires fetching the cached FFN input from memory to perform retrieval, introducing </span>Memory I/O overhead<span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> and pipeline stalls (<math id="A3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.182" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.182</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.182</annotation></semantics></math>s, <math id="A3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+13.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">13.0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+13.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>). Injecting into the current Self-Attention (SA) is even costlier (<math id="A3.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.195" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.195</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.195</annotation></semantics></math>s, <math id="A3.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+21.1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">21.1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+21.1\%</annotation></semantics></math>) as modifying the SA output necessitates a </span>re-computation<span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> of the subsequent FFN block. In contrast, our <span id="A3.I1.i2.p1.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Next Layer</span> design allows for a seamless “look-ahead” injection without backtracking or re-computation, achieving the optimal efficiency (<math id="A3.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.169" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.169</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.169</annotation></semantics></math>s, <math id="A3.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+5.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">+</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">5.0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+5.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(2) Why FFN over Self-Attention?<span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Comparing <span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Next Layer FFN</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="98.0\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">98.0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">98.0\%</annotation></semantics></math>) with <span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Next Layer SA</span> (<math id="A3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="97.3\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">97.3</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">97.3\%</annotation></semantics></math>) confirms that the FFN is the superior injection site. We hypothesize the reasons as follows: FFNs structurally function as </span>Key-Value Memories<span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Geva et al., 2021</a>; <a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jie et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, making them the natural component for retrieving and storing external information (observation). In contrast, Self-Attention focuses on token-to-token contextualization; injecting external features there may dilute the attention distribution, leading to slightly inferior performance.</span></span></p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T10" class="ltx_table">

<td id="A3.T10.6.1.5.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.5.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">95.8</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.5.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.5.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">97.7</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.5.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.5.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.182s</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.5.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.5.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">+13.0%</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T10.6.1.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Next Layer (</span><math id="A3.T10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathsize="0.900em" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo mathsize="0.900em">+</mo><mn mathsize="0.900em">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">)</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Self-Attention (SA)</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">98.4</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">98.0</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">97.8</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">94.8</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">97.3</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">0.170s</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.6.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.6.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">+5.6%</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T10.6.1.7" class="ltx_tr" style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">Next Layer (<math id="A3.T10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;" mathbackground="#E6FFFF" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;" mathbackground="#E6FFFF">+</mo><mn style="--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;" mathbackground="#E6FFFF">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell+1</annotation></semantics></math>)</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">Feed-Forward (UAOR)</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">99.0</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">98.4</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">98.2</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">96.2</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">98.0</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">0.169s</span></td>
<td id="A3.T10.6.1.7.9" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T10.6.1.7.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;--ltx-bg-color:#E6FFFF;">+5.0%</span></td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Visualizations of Simulation and Real-World Results</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We present additional qualitative results in both simulation and real-world settings to showcase the effectiveness of <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span>. All experiments are conducted within the OpenVLA-OFT framework. As illustrated in Figure <a href="#A4.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ Appendix D Theoretical Complexity Analysis ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and Figure <a href="#A4.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ Appendix D Theoretical Complexity Analysis ‣ UaOR: Uncertainty-aware Observation Reinjection for Vision-Language-Action Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, the model successfully completes diverse multi-stage manipulation tasks under varying object configurations and instruction formulations. Benefiting from the uncertainty-aware reinjection mechanism, <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> helps the model maintain focused attention on key observations during inference, enhancing scene understanding and decision confidence. These visualizations highlight the practicality and adaptability of our method in robotic manipulation.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span><span id="A4.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Theoretical Complexity Analysis</span></h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For simplicity, we only consider the computational overhead of the Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) and Feed-Forward Network (FFN) blocks in a language model backbone. Let <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>D</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D</annotation></semantics></math> denote the number of transformer layers, the length of the token sequence, and the hidden dimension, respectively. Following prior works <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jie et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025a</a>; <a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2025b</a>)</cite>, the floating-point operations (FLOPs) for MHSA and FFN in one layer are approximately <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8ND^{2}+4N^{2}D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8ND^{2}+4N^{2}D</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="16ND^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16ND^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively. Thus, the total FLOPs of the language model backbone are:</p>
<table id="A4.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{LM}}\approx L\cdot\left[(8ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)+16ND^{2}\right]=L\cdot(24ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>FLOPs</mtext><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">LM</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{LM}}\approx L\cdot\left[(8ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)+16ND^{2}\right]=L\cdot(24ND^{2}+4N^{2}D).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The additional computational overhead introduced by <span id="A4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> consists of two parts: (1) the <span id="A4.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">projection cost</span> to compute action entropy, and (2) the <span id="A4.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">reinjection cost</span> when uncertainty exceeds the threshold.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Projection Cost.</span> To compute the action entropy, we project the hidden states of action-related tokens into the vocabulary space using the pre-trained LM head. Let <math id="A4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the number of action-related tokens per step and <math id="A4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> the vocabulary size. Since we perform this projection at every layer except the last (where we don’t need to reinject at the next layer as it is just the last year), the additional FLOPs are:</p>
<table id="A4.E18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{proj}}=(L-1)\cdot 2N_{a}DD_{v}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>FLOPs</mtext><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">proj</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{proj}}=(L-1)\cdot 2N_{a}DD_{v}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reinjection Cost.</span> When triggered, <span id="A4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> acts as an additional FFN-like module comprising a retrieval operation. It involves two linear transformations (Query-Key and Attention-Value) with shared weights. Let <math id="A4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> be the number of observation tokens. The cost for a single reinjection is <math id="A4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{single\_inj}}\approx 4NN_{o}D" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mtext>FLOPs</mtext><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">single_inj</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{single\_inj}}\approx 4NN_{o}D</annotation></semantics></math>.
Assuming the reinjection is triggered in <math id="A4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math> layers (where uncertainty <math id="A4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u&gt;\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u&gt;\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>), the total reinjection cost is:</p>
<table id="A4.E19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{inj}}=L_{\gamma}\cdot 4NN_{o}D." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mtext>FLOPs</mtext><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{inj}}=L_{\gamma}\cdot 4NN_{o}D.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(19)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Total Overhead Ratio.</span> We quantify the additional computational burden using the ratio <math id="A4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\text{cost}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>cost</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{cost}}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A4.E20" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\text{cost}}=\frac{\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{proj}}+\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{inj}}}{\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{LM}}}\approx\underbrace{\frac{(L-1)\cdot 2N_{a}DD_{v}}{L\cdot(24ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)}}_{\text{Projection term}}+\underbrace{\frac{L_{\gamma}\cdot 4NN_{o}D}{L\cdot(24ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)}}_{\text{Reinjection term}}." display="block" class="ltx_font_smallcaps">proj</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mtext>FLOPs</mtext><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">inj</mtext></msub></mrow><msub><mtext>FLOPs</mtext><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">LM</mtext></msub></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Projection term</mtext></munder><mo>+</mo><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mfrac><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>Reinjection term</mtext></munder></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{cost}}=\frac{\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{proj}}+\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{inj}}}{\text{FLOPs}_{\textsc{LM}}}\approx\underbrace{\frac{(L-1)\cdot 2N_{a}DD_{v}}{L\cdot(24ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)}}_{\text{Projection term}}+\underbrace{\frac{L_{\gamma}\cdot 4NN_{o}D}{L\cdot(24ND^{2}+4N^{2}D)}}_{\text{Reinjection term}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(20)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Note that we approximate the denominator by the dominant term <math id="A4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="24ND^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24ND^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (since <math id="A4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D\gg N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>≫</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D\gg N</annotation></semantics></math>) for clarity.
Simplifying the terms yields:</p>
<table id="A4.E21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{\text{cost}}\approx\frac{N_{a}D_{v}}{12ND}+\frac{L_{\gamma}}{L}\cdot\frac{N_{o}}{6D}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mtext>cost</mtext></msub><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mi>L</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>D</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{\text{cost}}\approx\frac{N_{a}D_{v}}{12ND}+\frac{L_{\gamma}}{L}\cdot\frac{N_{o}}{6D}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(21)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case Study.</span> We analyze the overhead for two representative VLA models, OpenVLA-OFT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kim et al., 2025a</a>)</cite> and CogACT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite>, using the Llama-2-7B backbone (<math id="A4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D=4096,D_{v}=32000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>32000</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D=4096,D_{v}=32000</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
<ul id="A4.I1" class="ltx_itemize" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:10pt;">
<li id="A4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">OpenVLA-OFT</span>: With sequence length <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\approx 600" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>600</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\approx 600</annotation></semantics></math> and action tokens <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}=56" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>56</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}=56</annotation></semantics></math>, the projection overhead is <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx\frac{56\times 32000}{12\times 600\times 4096}\approx\textbf{6.0\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>56</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32000</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>600</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">6.0%</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx\frac{56\times 32000}{12\times 600\times 4096}\approx\textbf{6.0\%}</annotation></semantics></math>. On LIBERO-Long, the statistical trigger rate is <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{L_{\gamma}}{L}\approx 20\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>γ</mi></msub><mi>L</mi></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{L_{\gamma}}{L}\approx 20\%</annotation></semantics></math>. With observation tokens <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{o}=513" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>513</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{o}=513</annotation></semantics></math>, the reinjection overhead is <math id="A4.I1.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.2\times\frac{513}{6\times 4096}\approx\textbf{0.4\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0.2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mfrac><mn>513</mn><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">0.4%</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.2\times\frac{513}{6\times 4096}\approx\textbf{0.4\%}</annotation></semantics></math>. The total overhead is roughly <span id="A4.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">6.4%</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">CogACT</span>: With <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\approx 300" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>300</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\approx 300</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{a}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{a}=1</annotation></semantics></math> (predicting one condition token per step), the projection overhead drops significantly to <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx\frac{1\times 32000}{12\times 300\times 4096}\approx\textbf{0.2\%}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>32000</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>300</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_bold">0.2%</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx\frac{1\times 32000}{12\times 300\times 4096}\approx\textbf{0.2\%}</annotation></semantics></math>. Assuming a similar trigger rate, the total overhead remains negligible at <math id="A4.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;1\%</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="A4.p5.2" class="ltx_p">This analysis confirms that <span id="A4.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> is computationally efficient, particularly for those VLA models that generate one action-related token per step, and introduces minimal latency compared to the heavy backbone computation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18020v1/simulation.png" id="A4.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:476/570;" width="476" height="570" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="A4.F6.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Manipulation Visualizations in the LIBERO Simulation Environment.<span id="A4.F6.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> We present the execution processes of OpenVLA-OFT with <span id="A4.F6.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> across LIBERO-Spatial, LIBERO-Object, LIBERO-Goal, and LIBERO-Long, demonstrating its strong performance under diverse instructions and a wide range of tasks. Each row shows a temporally ordered sequence from left to right.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A4.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18020v1/real.png" id="A4.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:452/603;" width="452" height="603" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F7.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A4.F7.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Manipulation Visualizations in the Real-World Environment.<span id="A4.F7.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> We present the execution processes of OpenVLA-OFT with <span id="A4.F7.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">UaOR</span> across four real-world tasks, demonstrating its strong effectiveness and practicality in real-world scenarios. Each pair of rows shows a temporally ordered sequence from left to right.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
